- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.32) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If model shows strong upward trend after a recent spike, check for lag: true price often corrects 1–2 days later — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 3+ days, model often underestimates downside — add 2–5% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion or volatility.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon — especially after high sentiment spikes — apply 3–5% downward correction for first 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after model peak, assume sentiment shift — reduce forecast for next 3–5 days by 3–7% to reflect sentiment decay.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment direction, not just price history.
